requirements_summary:
- Workloads: chat-based support assistant (50 concurrent agents peak), embeddings for semantic search (nightly reindex), reranking for top-N results, occasional code-assist sessions.
- Latency targets: chat p95 <= 150ms for short-turn replies; embeddings bulk throughput 80–120 reqs/s during batch windows.
- Cost sensitivity: target 20% lower unit cost vs. VendorX for the same quality.
- Model preferences: prefer open/compatible model variants; need ability to pin model versions and automatic fallback to smaller model when Dedicated capacity constrained.
- Operational: want request-level tracing, token-level billing, and per-route dashboards. Must have SSO + role-based access and audit logs.
poc_summary:
- Approach: mapped existing OpenAI ChatCompletions traffic through an internal compat shim to Redwood Hosted chat endpoint to compare outputs side-by-side.
- Findings: tokenization differences and system-message handling caused several prompts to change structure; function-calling produced different argument orders in 7% of cases.
- Regression example: a 10-step troubleshooting flow where Redwood-hosted replies collapsed two steps into one, breaking our downstream UI step tracker; happened in ~3% of test set.
- Ops: Hosted endpoints achieved median latency of ~90ms but p95 spiked to 210ms under burst load; SE recommended Dedicated for stable p95 and autoscaling.
- Mitigations: suggested fixes include prompt canonicalization, explicit function schemas, pinning model revision, and running Redwood Optimize suggestions on batching/kv cache.
